title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: Work IQ API access to declarative agents
summary: Hold: the spending-policy update call changes limits and billing methods, but does not configure the users or service access promised by its control row. Most of the briefing is supported; it also needs to acknowledge Microsoft's differing guidance on automatic service-principal provisioning and narrow its statements about unpublished pricing and agent access.

claims.claim: Applications can programmatically access first-party and tenant-defined declarative agents through the Work IQ endpoint for domain-specific workflow tasks.
claims.quote: Enables programmatic access to first‑party and tenant‑defined declarative agents via the Work IQ endpoint, allowing applications to trigger specialized agents for domain‑specific tasks within broader workflows.

claims.claim: Work IQ is admin-opt-in and an administrator must enable it before applications can use it.
claims.quote: An organization administrator must enable Work IQ in your organization before these permissions can be used by applications.
claims.fix: Keep admin-opt-in for the documented billing and consent prerequisites, but replace the absolute manual-enablement wording in the summary, Why it matters, Scope and risk rationale with 'Work IQ API use requires admin-approved permissions and configured usage-based billing.' Add 'The permissions and setup pages require tenant enablement, while the MCP overview says the service principal is created automatically on first use and manual provisioning is needed in some corner cases.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/overview.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Learn billing pages publish no numerical credit rate for Work IQ API requests at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ API requests Copilot Credits rate licensing pricing; Work IQ API credit rate 0.1 tools pricing requests licensing. Read overview, api-overview, cost-considerations and billing overview. Microsoft licensing news separately publishes a Tool API rate and variable Chat/Context consumption.
claims.fix: Replace the broad rate-gap statements with 'The cited Learn pages do not give a fixed credit rate for requests to declarative agents. Microsoft's pricing announcement describes Work IQ Chat and Context consumption as variable.' Cite https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/licensing/news/work-iq-general-availability; do not imply that Microsoft has published no Work IQ pricing.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management is where administrators manage Work IQ API spending controls.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with ... Work IQ API.
claims.fix: Keep the path, which reaches the correct dashboard, and clarify in the note: 'Cost management is the dashboard entry point; use its Configuration experience to configure spending policies, covered services, limits and billing methods.'

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} configures who can use Work IQ API as well as how much they can spend.
claims.quote: The audience type can't be changed by updating a policy. ... Apply limits to selected security groups ... add ... assigned groups ... Configure the services governed by the policy ... spendingPolicyServiceSetting
claims.fix: Narrow controls[2].governs to 'Spending limits and billing methods for an existing Work IQ API spending policy'. Keep the PATCH call and add to its note: 'This operation updates limits and billing methods; user/group assignments and service access use separate operations.' Make the rendered row match. The update reference permits displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods, not audience assignments or Work IQ service selection.
